name: Catalina 30 Mk II
notes: All points are pixels in the 600x948 drawing, read by hand off gridded enlargements and snapped to dark pixels where a column scan found the line. Bow is to the right in both views.

The Mk I drawing on https://sailboatdata.com/sailboat/catalina-30/ stops at the waterline, so it cannot give draft; the Mk II (1986-91) is the same hull with a new deck, cockpit and liner, and its drawing shows the fin keel and spade rudder. The deep fin is drawn solid; the dashed outline inside it is the optional wing keel and is not traced.
The drawing puts the accommodation plan over the sail plan's luff, on the same x scale as the profile: the plan's stern sits at x 15, the profile's transom at x 16.

Profile hull, transom top to stem head, spans x 16 to 563 = 547 px for an LOA of 29.92 ft, 18.28 px/ft. Draft reads 5.55 ft against a published 5.25 (+6%); beam reads 10.9 ft against 10.83. The vertical scale is not off: I reads about 41.8 ft against 41.0. The keel is drawn deep.
The drawn waterline at y 838.5 sits under a boot top whose top edge is level at y 831.
The rig reads J 13.1 ft and P 36.5 ft, between the standard rig (J 11.5, P 35) and the tall rig in the page's notes (J 13.16, P 37). It is traced as drawn.

Inferred: forward of plan x 524 the drawn deck runs on to a point at x 578, 15 px past the profile's stem head; the pulpit and stemhead fitting are drawn continuous with the deck edge. The deck is closed to the stem head at x 563 by hand; the points from x 534 on are a guess, not a trace. Aft, the plan's transom is a convex arc and the two points aft of x 24 follow it by eye.
